components.name: AiLabel
components.summary: Marks content as made by AI, and on request says why. Given an explanation, the mark is a button that opens a short note right under it, with an optional list of sources. It is a disclosure (a button that shows and hides a region), not a tooltip or a popover: a tooltip can't hold links and never shows on a touch screen, and the system has no popover.
components.useWhen: Marking a block of text, a value or a field that an AI wrote, so the person knows to check it.

props.name: label
props.description: The mark's words, and the button's name. Say what the AI made: 'AI summary', 'AI draft'.

props.name: explanation
props.description: Why this is AI content and what to do about it, in a sentence or two: what it was made from, and that it needs checking. Without it the mark is static text and nothing opens.

props.name: sources
props.description: { label, href } for each thing the content was made from. Listed under the explanation; ignored without one.

props.name: renderLink
props.description: How each source link is drawn. Pass your router's link component for sources inside the app.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the root's classes. When Tailwind utility classes clash, the later one wins.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the root div.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native attribute, onto the root div.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A small square that shows who someone is. The name is required, because it's both the alt text (the description screen readers read for an image) and the source of the initials. Without one, an avatar is just an image nobody can identify.
components.useWhen: Showing who a person is, next to their name, as in a roster row, a comment or an account menu.

props.name: name
props.description: Required. The source of the fallback initials and the announced name.

props.name: src
props.description: Optional image. If it can't load, the fallback takes its place without the layout jumping.

props.name: status
props.description: Whether the person is around. It adds the dot and adds the word to the announced name. Leave it out when you don't know.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component's classes. When Tailwind utility classes clash, the later one wins.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the root element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native span prop except aria-label and children. aria-label is removed from the types rather than quietly overwritten when the page runs. The announced name comes from the sr-only span, and an aria-label on the root would override it. children is removed because the component renders its own image/fallback/sr-only children, so anything passed as children would silently disappear.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A small chip that shows a status. It comes in six tones and two emphases, and it always carries a word. A colour on its own isn't a status anyone can read.
components.useWhen: You need to label a status with a word and a tone, like an order state or a sync result.

props.name: tone
props.description: The status the badge shows.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: Solid uses the invariant fill (the same in light and dark themes) with its matching ink. Subtle is the outline badge: a 1px border and text in the tone’s theme-adaptive text token, with no fill. There's no separate outline emphasis, because it would be this same look under a second name.

props.name: size
props.description: sm (small) is the chip for everyday interface: rows, cards, tables. md (medium) takes the small control height (32px) and the 14px text step. Use it for a badge next to display-size type, like a price.

props.name: dot
props.description: Adds a marker next to the text.

props.name: icon
props.description: An icon before the text, hidden from screen readers with aria-hidden and sized to the badge. It takes the badge’s colour, so the same contrast pair that covers the text covers it too. It adds to the word. It never replaces it.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component classes. If two clash, the later Tailwind utility wins (Tailwind is the CSS framework this system styles with).

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the span element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Any other span attribute. For example, aria-hidden on a count that a label next to it already reads out.

components.name: Button
components.summary: The main control for taking an action. It comes in five variants (one of them a button that looks like a text link) and four sizes, with optional icons on either side of the label. It also draws its own focus ring, the outline that shows which control the keyboard is on. The component places that ring for you, because the bevel (the cut corners) would clip one placed anywhere else.
components.useWhen: An action on this page, like submit, save or open a dialog.

props.name: variant
props.description: Which fill/border treatment to use. link looks like a Link (signal text, underline, no fill, no bevel, no fixed height) but it's still a button. Use it for an action inside a sentence, not for going to another page.

props.name: size
props.description: 24 / 32 / 40 / 48px (pixels). xs is exactly the 24px minimum target, the smallest area people can reliably click or tap. It isn't a token step (there is no xs control-height token) and it's meant for dense toolbars and table rows. Size has no effect on the link variant, which takes the size of the text around it.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the wrapper as well as the button.

props.name: loading
props.description: Sets aria-busy and aria-disabled, blocks the click and the form submit, and shows the spinner. The button stays focusable.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: Text that's hidden on screen but read aloud while loading.

props.name: iconStart
props.description: An icon before the label, rendered aria-hidden and sized to the button. The spinner replaces it while loading. It isn't available with asChild: put the icon inside the child element instead.

props.name: iconEnd
props.description: An icon after the label, rendered aria-hidden. It stays while loading. Not available with asChild.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Renders the child element with the button's classes. Use it for links that look like buttons. Combining it with disabled, loading or loadingLabel is a type error, so the code won't compile, instead of quietly doing nothing. A link can't really be disabled or made busy, so those props are removed from the types rather than ignored when the page runs.

props.name: wrapperClassName
props.description: Classes for the focus wrapper, not the button.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component's classes. When Tailwind utility classes clash, the later one wins.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the button element.

props.name: type
props.description: A Button never submits a form by accident. Ask for submit on the one that should.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native button prop except aria-busy. aria-busy is removed from the types rather than quietly overwritten when the page runs. loading is the only thing that sets it, and a loading button saying aria-busy="false" would be a spinning, aria-disabled control telling assistive tech (screen readers and other tools people with disabilities use) that it's idle. children is its own declared prop above, not part of rest.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A checkbox with three states: off, on and mixed. Radix (the open-source library of accessible building blocks underneath it) handles the semantics and the keyboard behaviour. The look comes from the system's shape language: a square with no rounding and a tick in ink.
components.useWhen: An on/off choice that applies when the form is saved, or a parent whose children are partly selected.

props.name: checked
props.description: The checked state, when your code controls it.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: The starting state when the checkbox manages itself (uncontrolled). It's narrower than Radix's own boolean | 'indeterminate'. The tick or dash can only follow a checked value the caller passed in. Radix would track an uncontrolled mixed state internally but never hand it back, so that state is excluded instead of being drawn with the wrong mark.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Runs every time it toggles.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Takes it out of the tab order and stops it toggling.

props.name: required
props.description: Uses the browser's built-in form validation.

props.name: name
props.description: The field name sent with a native form.

props.name: value
props.description: The field value sent with a native form.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets aria-invalid (an ARIA attribute, from Accessible Rich Internet Applications, that tells screen readers the field has an error) and shows the invalid border.

props.name: id
props.description: Pair it with a real label through htmlFor.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the control's classes. If two clash, the later Tailwind utility wins (Tailwind is the CSS framework this system styles with).

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the Radix root button.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every Radix Checkbox.Root prop except aria-invalid, spread onto the root. aria-invalid is removed from the type, so you can't pass it, instead of being quietly overwritten while the page runs. invalid is the only thing that sets both the attribute and the border. defaultChecked is declared again above, narrowed to boolean.

components.name: Divider
components.summary: A thin line, with an optional legend (a short text label). When it's only decoration, screen readers skip it. When it marks where a section starts, it's a real separator they announce.
components.useWhen: A thin line between groups of content, labelled when it starts a new section.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which way the line runs.

props.name: label
props.description: Adds a legend and makes the divider more than decoration.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component's classes. When Tailwind utility classes clash, the later one wins.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the root element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native div prop except role and children. role is removed from the types rather than quietly overwritten when the page runs, because label already decides whether the divider is decorative or structural. children is removed because it behaved two different ways: with no label it rendered inside a decorative separator, and with one it disappeared.

components.name: IconButton
components.summary: A square button with one icon. It uses exactly the same variants as Button (same source code, so the two can't drift apart). It requires a label, because an icon on its own tells a screen reader nothing.
components.useWhen: An action shown as a single icon, with a label that names the action.

props.name: label
props.description: Required. It becomes aria-label. It's required in the types, so an icon button with no name won't compile.

props.name: variant
props.description: Which fill/border treatment to use. These are Button’s variants minus link, since an icon has no text to underline.

props.name: size
props.description: 32 / 40 / 48px (pixels), all above the 24px minimum target size, the smallest area people can reliably click or tap. Button’s xs isn't offered: 32px is the smallest this control goes.

props.name: count
props.description: A number in a corner badge, like items in a cart or unread notifications. It's added to the accessible name, the name screen readers announce (‘Notifications, 3 unread’). It shows as 99+ past 99 and is hidden at 0 unless showZero is set.

props.name: countLabel
props.description: Formats the spoken part of the name that comes after the label and a comma: count => `${count} unread`. It always gets the real number, never 99+.

props.name: showZero
props.description: Shows the badge when the count is 0.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Renders the child element with the button's classes. Use it for links that look like icon buttons. Combining it with disabled is a type error, so the code won't compile, instead of quietly doing nothing. A link can't really be disabled, so the prop is removed from the types rather than ignored when the page runs.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Left out on purpose. An icon button is always square, and stretching it would break that.

props.name: wrapperClassName
props.description: Classes for the focus wrapper, not the button.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component's classes. When Tailwind utility classes clash, the later one wins.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the button element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native button prop except aria-label. aria-label is removed from the types rather than quietly overwritten when the page runs. label is the only source of the accessible name, and an aria-label in rest would beat it. children is its own declared prop above, not part of rest.

components.name: Input
components.summary: A single-line text field. It doesn't label itself. The label, help text, error text and the wiring between them are FormField's job. On its own, Input handles the box, its states and the focus ring (the outline that shows which element the keyboard is on). It also has three optional extras inside its right edge: a password reveal, a character counter and a clear button.
components.useWhen: Single-line text, inside a FormField.

props.name: inputSize
props.description: Called inputSize because size is already a real HTML attribute on input.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets aria-invalid (an ARIA attribute, from Accessible Rich Internet Applications, that tells screen readers the field has an error) and shows the invalid border. It doesn't show any error text.

props.name: size
props.description: The browser's own attribute, still available.

props.name: revealable
props.description: On type="password", adds a Show password toggle with aria-pressed. The name stays the same, and the pressed state says whether the password is showing. It goes back to hidden when the form submits. Other types ignore it.

props.name: showCount
props.description: Works with maxLength. It shows 12/80 in mono inside the field and adds it to aria-describedby, the attribute that links extra description to a field. It's merged with any describedby you pass in, which is how FormField keeps its help and error text. It only announces the characters left near the limit (the last tenth, and at least the last three), through a polite live region, an area screen readers read out without interrupting.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Shows a clear button while the field has a value (never when it's disabled or read-only). Clearing fires onChange with an empty value, so a controlled field clears through its own handler. Then it calls onClear, then puts focus back in the input.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Called after the clear button empties the field.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: The clear button’s name. If the page has more than one, say what it clears: ‘Clear call sign’.

props.name: aiValue
props.description: The value an AI proposed. While the field holds exactly this value it shows the AI-filled state: an ai.border edge, a faint ai.wash tint and a sparkle mark that describes the field as Filled by AI. Once the person changes it, the field looks normal again and a Revert to suggestion button puts the value back through onChange (no button on a disabled or read-only field). An invalid field keeps its invalid border.

props.name: wrapperClassName
props.description: Classes for the wrapper a field with extras renders. Put width classes here when an extra is on. It does nothing on a bare input.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the input’s classes. If two clash, the later Tailwind utility wins (Tailwind is the CSS framework this system styles with).

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the input element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native input prop except aria-invalid, spread onto the element. aria-invalid is removed from the type, so you can't pass it, instead of being quietly overwritten while the page runs. invalid is the only thing that sets both the attribute and the border. If a caller could set one directly, what you see and what screen readers hear could drift apart. size is declared again above as the native number attribute, because inputSize controls the variant.

components.name: Kbd
components.summary: A small keycap that shows a key's name. Making shortcuts easy to find was one of the motifs from the G1 mood board (the project's first approval step) worth keeping: if a surface has a shortcut, the surface says so.
components.useWhen: Showing a keyboard shortcut next to the action it triggers, with one Kbd per key.

props.name: children
props.description: The key's name, for example "Esc" or "⌘".

props.name: size
props.description: md is 24px tall, for a cap beside text or in a menu row. sm is 20px tall, for a cap inside a 32px control: a small Button or a search field.

props.name: cut
props.description: Cuts the bottom-right corner (5px at sm, 8px at md) so the cap nests in the corner of a bevelled control, its diagonal parallel to the control's. Only for a cap inside such a control.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component's classes. When Tailwind utility classes clash, the later one wins.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the kbd element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native attribute, passed onto the kbd element, such as a title, or an aria-label for a symbol key (aria-label is the name screen readers read out).

components.name: Link
components.summary: A link inside text. It's underlined, because in a paragraph colour alone isn't enough to show that something is a link.
components.useWhen: Text that takes you somewhere: another page, a section or another site.

props.name: tone
props.description: Which colour treatment to use.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens the link in a new tab. It adds target="_blank", the rel hardening (attributes that stop the new page reaching back into yours), a trailing icon and the hidden "(opens in a new tab)" warning. Using it together with target or rel is a type error, so it can't fail silently. external already sets those values, so those props are removed from the type instead of being quietly overwritten while the page runs.

props.name: href
props.description: Where the link goes.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component classes. If two clash, the later Tailwind utility wins (Tailwind is the CSS framework this system styles with).

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the anchor element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native anchor prop.

components.name: LoadingAnimation
components.summary: A loading state that fills a whole panel, drawn as an animated instrument dial in WebGL (the browser's graphics engine for drawing with the graphics card). The three dials follow the same rules. They draw themselves from the outside in, and their structure drifts. One mechanism clicks to its next detent using the system's snap easing (the motion where things arrive a little large and settle), and the signal accent colour only appears on the part that shows progress.
components.useWhen: A wait that takes over a whole panel or page, like a route loading, a report building or a first sync.

props.name: variant
props.description: Aperture: shaded blades stepping round a spinning core. Gyro: nested rings turning against each other. Reticle: a progress ring filling up from a marker at 12 o’clock.

props.name: size
props.description: A 96px, 160px or 240px square (px means pixels). It shrinks with its container below that size, but never grows.

props.name: label
props.description: Status text that is hidden on screen. Passing it turns the loader into a live region, an area screen readers announce when it changes.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component classes. If two clash, the later Tailwind utility wins (Tailwind is the CSS framework this system styles with).

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the root div.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native div prop except role, for the same reason as Spinner: label is the only thing that sets role="status".

components.name: Panel
components.summary: The system's framed surface: a thin border around a fill, with the crosshair corner marks and the cut corner as options. Card is a Panel with a title, body and footer; Panel is the frame alone, for a feature tile, a demo frame or a tile that is one link.
components.useWhen: Framing content that has no title, body and footer structure: a feature tile, a demo area, or a tile that is one link.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner spacing: 0, 12px, 20px or 32px.

props.name: tone
props.description: base sits flush with the page, raised is one step up, signal is the brand wash for the one panel in a group that leads.

props.name: crosshair
props.description: Draws the crosshair marks at the corners.

props.name: cut
props.description: Cuts the bottom-right corner, with the border following the cut.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Hover and focus states for a panel that is one link or button. Use it with asChild; it adds no behaviour of its own.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Renders the single child element (an a, a router Link, a button) with the panel classes merged onto it, instead of a div.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component's classes. Use it for layout (a grid span, flex, gap), not for the fill or the border.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the div, or to the child with asChild.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native attribute, passed onto the element.

components.name: Progress
components.summary: A progress bar that's either determinate (it knows how far along the task is) or indeterminate (it doesn't). The readout is real text in the DOM (the Document Object Model, the live page structure the browser builds) from the very first render. That's motion token M3's rule, and it means a screen reader, the software that reads the page aloud for blind and low-vision people, never hears a number roll.
components.useWhen: Showing how far a measurable task has got. Switch to indeterminate once you no longer know how much is left.

props.name: label
props.description: Required. The bar’s accessible name.

props.name: value
props.description: null means indeterminate. The value is clamped to [0, max], so an out-of-range value shows as complete instead of overflowing the track.

props.name: max
props.description: The value at which the bar is complete.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the percentage (or "In progress") as a readout.

props.name: tone
props.description: The fill colour. signal paints accent.signal.indicator to match Slider. On the track in light theme that’s a 2.80:1 contrast ratio, below the 3:1 a bar needs when it’s the only sign of progress. So set showValue there.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the outer wrapper’s classes. Later Tailwind utilities (Tailwind is the CSS framework the system is styled with) win.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the Radix Progress root, which is the bar itself. Radix is the library of accessible building blocks this component sits on.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native div prop except children, spread onto the outer wrapper, so a molecule can attach a data-testid there. children is typed away because this component draws its own label row and track, and a children prop would be thrown away without any warning.

components.name: Radio
components.summary: Pick one choice from a set. The whole group is a single tab stop, and the arrow keys move inside it. That’s how native radio buttons behave, and it’s most of the reason this is built on a Radix primitive (Radix is a library of accessible building blocks) instead of three styled inputs.
components.useWhen: One choice from a short set, up to about seven, all shown at once.

props.name: value (RadioGroup)
props.description: The selected value, when you control it from outside.

props.name: defaultValue (RadioGroup)
props.description: The starting value, when the group manages it itself (uncontrolled).

props.name: onValueChange (RadioGroup)
props.description: Fires when the selection changes.

props.name: name (RadioGroup)
props.description: The native form field name.

props.name: required (RadioGroup)
props.description: Uses the browser’s native form validation.

props.name: disabled (RadioGroup)
props.description: Disables every option in the group.

props.name: orientation (RadioGroup)
props.description: Sets which arrow keys move between options. The visual layout is still up to className.

props.name: aria-label / aria-labelledby (RadioGroup)
props.description: One of these is required. They’re ARIA attributes (from Accessible Rich Internet Applications) that give the group a name screen readers announce. A radiogroup with no name is a bug.

props.name: value (Radio)
props.description: Required. This option’s value.

props.name: disabled (Radio)
props.description: Takes just this option out of selection.

props.name: id (Radio)
props.description: Pair it with a real label using htmlFor.

props.name: invalid (Radio)
props.description: Sets aria-invalid, which tells assistive tech the field has an error, and shows the invalid border.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the control's classes. Later Tailwind utilities (Tailwind is the CSS framework the system uses) win.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the Radix root element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every Radix RadioGroup.Item prop except aria-invalid, spread onto the item. aria-invalid is typed away instead of being quietly overridden at runtime, because invalid is the only source of both the attribute and the border. RadioGroup itself excludes nothing. It computes no value of its own that a rest prop could defeat.

components.name: ScoreRing
components.summary: One 0 to 100 score shown as a ring with the number in its centre, split into bands the way Lighthouse (Google’s website audit tool) bands its scores. It’s a meter, so a screen reader, the software that reads the page aloud, hears both the score and its band.
components.useWhen: A 0 to 100 score with good and bad bands, like an audit, a health check or a quality score. Several side by side read as one report.

props.name: label
props.description: Required. What’s being scored. It’s both the accessible name and the caption.

props.name: value
props.description: Required. 0 to 100, clamped and rounded to a whole number.

props.name: size
props.description: The ring is 56, 96 or 128px (pixels) wide.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the meter’s classes. Later Tailwind utilities (Tailwind is the CSS framework the system uses) win.

props.name: ref
props.description: Points to the meter.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native div prop except children, spread onto the meter. The ring draws its own content.

props.name: scoreBand()
props.description: The banding the ring uses. It’s exported so a table or a sentence beside the ring agrees with it.

components.name: Select
components.summary: A single choice from a list, shown in a portalled listbox (a pop-up list rendered at the top level of the page, so nothing around it can clip it). Options come in as an array instead of as children, because the trigger, the panel and the look of each row are decisions the system makes once, not per use.
components.useWhen: One choice from a list of about five options or more.

props.name: label
props.description: The trigger’s accessible name, the name a screen reader announces for it. Leave it out inside a FormField, which sets it from its own label. Outside one it is required, and `division-ds check` flags a missing one.

props.name: options
props.description: { value, label, disabled?, icon? } rows shown in the listbox. Pass this or groups, never both.

props.name: groups
props.description: { label, options }[]: rows under headings. Pass this or options, never both.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown until a value is chosen.

props.name: value
props.description: The selection, when you control it from outside. Following Radix’s own convention, pass it together with onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The starting selection, when the select manages it itself (uncontrolled). Pass this or value, never both.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the new value when a row is chosen, whether the select is controlled or uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the whole control.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the control as required for form submission.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name, for native form submission.

props.name: inputSize
props.description: Matches Input’s sizes so the two line up.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets aria-invalid, which tells assistive tech the field has an error, and shows the invalid border.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the trigger’s classes. Later Tailwind utilities (Tailwind is the CSS framework the system uses) win.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the trigger button.

props.name: id
props.description: The trigger’s id. FormField sets it.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: The ids of the help and error text, set on the trigger so a screen reader reads them with it. FormField sets it.

props.name: triggerProps
props.description: Extra props for the visible trigger button, e.g. data-testid. These are separate from the top-level rest, which goes to Radix’s Root (value, onValueChange, disabled, required, name, dir, form…) and never reaches an element on the page. aria-label and aria-invalid are typed away instead of being quietly overridden at runtime, because label and invalid already decide those.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Radix’s Root control props only. Every aria-* attribute and data-testid are typed away at the top level, because Root renders no element on the page, and anything that lands there vanishes with no error anywhere. Send them through triggerProps instead. children is typed away because this component renders its own Trigger and Portal.

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: A loading placeholder shaped like the content it stands in for: lines of text, a cut-corner block, or an Avatar’s footprint. The shapes themselves are silent. SkeletonGroup is what tells people the region is loading.
components.useWhen: A region whose content is loading, shown as placeholders in its shape inside one SkeletonGroup.

props.name: shape
props.description: What the placeholder stands in for.

props.name: lines
props.description: Text only. The number of lines. Anything below 1 counts as 1.

props.name: size
props.description: Avatar only. Matches Avatar’s size prop.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component classes. A block takes its width and height from here.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the root element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native div prop except children, because a skeleton draws its own shapes.

props.name: label (SkeletonGroup)
props.description: The hidden words a screen reader hears instead of the shapes.

props.name: className (SkeletonGroup)
props.description: Lay the placeholders out here, the way the real content will be laid out.

props.name: ref (SkeletonGroup)
props.description: Passed through to the container.

props.name: ...rest (SkeletonGroup)
props.description: Every native div prop.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: A value or a range picked on a track. Each thumb (the handle you drag) gets its own name. If a range slider shared one name, a screen-reader user (someone using software that reads the page aloud) would get two controls called the same thing.
components.useWhen: A value or range on a track, where the rough position matters and the value is shown.

props.name: label
props.description: Required. Applied to each thumb. A single thumb gets it as-is, and a range adds "minimum" / "maximum" to the end.

props.name: value
props.description: The value(s), when you control them from outside. One number makes a single slider; two make a range.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The starting value(s), when the slider manages them itself (uncontrolled).

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires as the thumb moves.

props.name: min
props.description: The lowest value.

props.name: max
props.description: The highest value.

props.name: step
props.description: The increment for both snapping while dragging and the arrow keys.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Takes it out of the tab order and blocks input.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: One function feeds both the readout and aria-valuetext (the ARIA, or Accessible Rich Internet Applications, attribute a screen reader speaks as the value). So the spoken value and the printed one can’t drift apart, whether the slider is controlled or not.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the current value(s) as a readout.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the outer wrapper's classes. Later Tailwind utilities (Tailwind is the CSS framework the system uses) win.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the Radix Slider root. Radix is the library of accessible building blocks this sits on.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every Radix Slider.Root prop except those three, spread onto the root. aria-label and aria-labelledby are left out because the accessible name lives on each thumb, where label puts it. One on the root would do nothing at all, not override anything. children is typed away because this component draws its own Track/Range/Thumbs, and a children prop would be thrown away without any warning.

components.name: Sparkline
components.summary: A small trend line with no axes. It sits beside a Stat or in a table cell. It's plain SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics, the web's format for drawn shapes): one image named by a sentence, with an optional safe band behind it and a square on the last value.
components.useWhen: You want the shape of a recent series, not its values. Think of a reading over the last hour.

props.name: values
props.description: Required. Oldest first. Non-finite values (such as NaN or Infinity) are dropped.

props.name: label
props.description: Required. The chart as one sentence: "Temperature, last hour: 3.1 to 4.2 °C, rising".

props.name: tone
props.description: The line's colour. Each tone means what it means on Badge.

props.name: min
props.description: A fixed bottom for the scale. Without it, the scale follows the data (and the band).

props.name: max
props.description: A fixed top for the scale. Without it, the scale follows the data (and the band).

props.name: band
props.description: A range drawn behind the line.

props.name: showLast
props.description: Puts a square on the last value.

props.name: width
props.description: In CSS px, the pixel unit of Cascading Style Sheets. className="w-full" overrides it.

props.name: height
props.description: In CSS px.

props.name: className
props.description: Goes on the frame.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the frame.

components.name: Spinner
components.summary: A busy indicator for an indeterminate wait, meaning one with no known end or percentage. It comes in two forms. The ring has a lit arc that grows and slides as it turns. The conveyor is a row of shaded blocks, for a wait that sits inside a line of text.
components.useWhen: A short wait with no known end, inside a control or a line of text.

props.name: variant
props.description: The rotating ring, or the block conveyor.

props.name: size
props.description: Ring: a 14px, 20px or 24px (pixel) box. Conveyor: 12px, 14px or 16px glyphs.

props.name: label
props.description: Status text that's hidden on screen. Passing it makes the spinner a live region, an area whose changes screen readers announce on their own.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component's classes. Later Tailwind utilities (the small styling classes this system uses) win.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the span element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native span prop except role, spread onto the span. role is removed from the type instead of being quietly overridden at runtime. Here's why: label is the only source of role="status", and a role in rest would silence the live region a caller asked for when they passed label.

components.name: Switch
components.summary: An on/off control that acts right away. The thumb's position shows the state, so the meaning still comes through with colour turned off. It takes effect the moment it's flipped.
components.useWhen: An on/off setting that takes effect the moment it's flipped.

props.name: checked
props.description: The checked state, when your code controls it.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: The starting state, when the switch manages itself.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Fires the moment it's flipped.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Takes it out of the tab order and blocks toggling.

props.name: required
props.description: The browser's own form validation.

props.name: name
props.description: The browser's own form field name.

props.name: value
props.description: The browser's own form field value.

props.name: id
props.description: Pair it with a real label through htmlFor.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the control's classes. Later Tailwind utilities (the small styling classes this system uses) win.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the root button from Radix, the open-source library this switch is built on.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every other Radix Switch.Root prop, which means every native button attribute, spread onto the root button. For example aria-describedby, or aria-label when no label element points at it. aria-* attributes are ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) settings that give screen readers extra information.

components.name: Tag
components.summary: A removable chip for filters and selections. Its dismiss button is named after the thing it removes, so a row of them doesn't sound like six identical 'Remove' buttons to a screen reader.
components.useWhen: A removable chip, such as an active filter or a selected value.

props.name: children
props.description: The tag text. Required.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Adds the dismiss button. It runs once the tag has faded out, not on the click. Remove the tag from your list here, and the tags after it slide into its place (M7, a motion token). With reduced motion turned on, it runs at once.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: Replaces the built dismiss name, for example with another verb or another language.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the component's classes. Later Tailwind utilities (the small styling classes this system uses) win.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the span element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native span attribute except children, spread onto the root span.

components.name: Textarea
components.summary: A text box for several lines. It has the same chrome (border, fill and states) as Input, resizes vertically and shows four rows by default. Like Input, it doesn't label itself.
components.useWhen: Free text over several lines, inside a FormField.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Sets aria-invalid and the invalid border. aria-invalid is an ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) attribute that tells screen readers the value has a problem. It doesn't render error text.

props.name: rows
props.description: The browser's own rows attribute. Size it to the answer you expect.

props.name: aiValue
props.description: The value an AI proposed, with the same contract as Input. The mark and the revert button sit in the top right corner. While the field holds exactly this value it shows the AI-filled state: an ai.border edge, a faint ai.wash tint and a sparkle mark that describes the field as Filled by AI. Once the person changes it, the field looks normal again and a Revert to suggestion button puts the value back through onChange (no button on a disabled or read-only field). An invalid field keeps its invalid border.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the control's classes. Later Tailwind utilities (the small styling classes this system uses) win.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the textarea element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every native textarea prop except aria-invalid, spread onto the element. aria-invalid is removed from the type instead of being quietly overridden at runtime. invalid is the only source of both the attribute and the border, so letting a caller set one directly would let what people see and what screen readers hear drift apart.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: Extra text that shows on hover or focus. It never holds information people can only get there. It doesn't appear on touch screens, it goes away, and someone may never trigger it.
components.useWhen: Extra detail on hover or focus for an element that can take focus, such as an IconButton.

props.name: content
props.description: Required. The extra text.

props.name: children
props.description: A single element that can take focus.

props.name: side
props.description: Which side of the trigger the content opens on.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the content’s classes. Later Tailwind utilities (the small styling classes this system uses) win.

components.name: Accordion
components.summary: Sections that open and close in place, each under its own heading. You can allow one open at a time or several, and draw them as plain rows split by thin lines or as a panel per section.
components.useWhen: Sections people scan by heading and open one or two of: frequently asked questions (FAQ), grouped settings, long specifications.

props.name: type
props.description: Required on the root. single: opening one section closes the other. multiple: any number can be open.

props.name: collapsible
props.description: single mode only. Lets the open section be closed again by its own trigger. You'll want it almost always.

props.name: variant
props.description: plain: thin separator lines, for a long run of questions. boxed: a panel per section, for a few sections that each stand alone.

props.name: value (Root)
props.description: The open section when the page controls it: a string in single mode, an array in multiple mode.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The section or sections open at first, when the accordion keeps track itself (uncontrolled). Set on the root.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when a section opens or closes (on the root). The argument has the same shape as type.

props.name: value (Item)
props.description: Required. The section’s own value.

props.name: disabled (Item)
props.description: The section can't be opened or closed.

props.name: level (Trigger)
props.description: The level of the heading the trigger sits in. Pick one below the heading the accordion appears under.

props.name: forceMount (Content)
props.description: Keeps a closed panel in the page's code (the DOM, the browser's live model of the page), so the browser's find-in-page search can reach its content. It then skips the closing animation.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with each part’s classes. On AccordionContent it goes on the inner padded box, not the animated clipping box around it.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the DOM element. Every part has one; the trigger’s is the button.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: A message that sits in the page. It shows its tone three ways, as an icon, a word and a colour, so it still reads on a greyscale screen and through a screen reader.
components.useWhen: A message that sits in the page and stays there: a warning about this screen, or a failed load with a retry.

props.name: tone
props.description: Which colour, icon and word the alert carries.

props.name: title
props.description: Required. Screen readers hear the tone word in front of it.

props.name: children
props.description: The body text.

props.name: live
props.description: Only for an alert added after the page has loaded. It sets the role screen readers use to announce it: hostile and warning get role=alert (announced at once), info and ok get role=status (announced politely).

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Adds the dismiss button. It runs once the alert has faded and its height has collapsed (M7), not on the click itself, so remove the alert from the page here. With reduced motion it runs straight away.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: The name screen readers give the dismiss button.

props.name: action
props.description: For example, a small Button.

props.name: compact
props.description: One line, for a toolbar, table header or card. The body sits inside the title paragraph, so pass plain inline text, not blocks.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the root.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the root DOM element.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: You can't set role yourself: live decides it.

components.name: ApprovalRequest
components.summary: A pause before an action that changes something in the real world (a side effect). It shows a preview of exactly what will happen, Approve and Reject buttons, and then a status line that takes keyboard focus.
components.useWhen: An assistant is about to send, change or spend something outside the conversation.

props.name: title
props.description: Required. The action as a question. It also names the section.

props.name: state
props.description: Required. Pending shows the buttons; approved or rejected shows the status line.

props.name: onApprove
props.description: Required. Run the action, then set state to approved.

props.name: onReject
props.description: Required. Set state to rejected. Nothing else happens.

props.name: approveLabel
props.description: The approve button. Say the action, like "Send".

props.name: rejectLabel
props.description: The reject button, like "Don't send".

props.name: approvedLabel
props.description: The status line once approved.

props.name: rejectedLabel
props.description: The status line once rejected.

props.name: className
props.description: Goes on the section.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.summary: Overlapping avatars (small profile pictures) with a “+N” for the rest. It’s a list named by its count, so a screen reader hears “6 members” and then each person. The people behind the “+N” are named in words, never only counted.
components.useWhen: Several people in one place, with a count: a squad, the people on an order, who’s viewing.

props.name: people
props.description: Required. Everyone in the group, in the order shown.

props.name: max
props.description: The most avatars drawn. The rest go into the +N chip.

props.name: size
props.description: Passed to every Avatar and to the chip.

props.name: label
props.description: What the group is. The count is added on the end: “Alpha squad, 6 members”.

props.name: overflowTooltip
props.description: Shows the hidden names in a Tooltip on the chip and lets the chip take keyboard focus.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged with the list classes. Later Tailwind utility classes win.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the list.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Every standard ul prop except children (the people are the content) and aria-label (label builds it, with the count).

props.name: name (AvatarGroupPerson)
props.description: Required. Passed to Avatar.

props.name: src (AvatarGroupPerson)
props.description: Optional image, passed to Avatar.

props.name: status (AvatarGroupPerson)
props.description: Optional presence (whether they’re online), passed to Avatar, which includes it in the name screen readers hear.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.summary: Shows where this page sits among the pages above it. The last level is the current page, shown as text. Every level above it is a link.
components.useWhen: Showing where a page sits in a hierarchy more than one level deep.

props.name: items
props.description: { label, href? }. A level with no href shows as plain text.

props.name: maxItems
props.description: Collapse the trail when it has more levels than this. It never goes below 3.

props.name: label
props.description: The name of the nav landmark.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the nav.

props.name: renderLink
props.description: How each linked level is drawn. Pass your router's link component to move between pages inside the app.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the nav DOM element.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A surface that groups related content. It gets the crosshair corners, the visual mark this system uses for a frame around several things. It never gets the cut corner, because cards hold buttons.
components.useWhen: Grouping related content on one surface, or one item in a grid whose whole surface is one link.

props.name: as
props.description: article for an item that stands on its own, section for a group inside a page, div for neither.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Says the whole card is one click target, through a link or button stretched over it. Adds the hover and focus border and a 4px lift. It adds no role and no Tab stop: the link inside is still the control.

props.name: level (CardTitle)
props.description: The heading level, set on CardTitle only. Card itself takes no level. The page decides its own outline.

props.name: src (CardMedia)
props.description: The picture, drawn with object-cover (it fills the box and crops the overflow) and loaded lazily (only when it's about to scroll into view). Leave it out to show CardMedia's children instead, such as a placeholder.

props.name: alt (CardMedia)
props.description: The alt text screen readers read for the picture. Empty by default: the picture is decorative because the card title already names it. Write real text only when the picture says something the title doesn't.

props.name: aspect (CardMedia)
props.description: The shape of the box the picture is cropped to.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto any part.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Standard HTML attributes on every part, except aria-labelledby on Card: the Card points that at its CardTitle itself, and the types won't accept one passed in. Give CardTitle an id only if something else needs it.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the Card root DOM element.

components.name: ChatMessage
components.summary: One turn in a conversation with an assistant: the person's words in a bubble, the reply at full width, or a centred system line. While a reply is still streaming in, it sets aria-busy (an ARIA, Accessible Rich Internet Applications, attribute that tells screen readers the content isn't finished) and shows a caret that doesn't blink.
components.useWhen: Each turn inside a ChatThread.

props.name: role
props.description: Required. Who's speaking. system is a quiet, centred status line.

props.name: author
props.description: Required. "You", "Assistant". It names the message.

props.name: time
props.description: The date and time in ISO format (the international standard way of writing them), for <time dateTime>.

props.name: timeLabel
props.description: The time as shown on screen: "09:40".

props.name: streaming
props.description: The text is still arriving: sets aria-busy and shows a caret. Inside a ChatThread, the finished text is announced once, when this turns false.

props.name: actions
props.description: Small buttons under an assistant message. They aren't shown on a user message.

props.name: className
props.description: Goes on the article.

props.name: onSubmit (ResponseFeedback)
props.description: Required. Runs on a thumbs up or down. Return a promise to show "Submitting feedback" until it settles; a rejection puts the buttons back.

props.name: onDetail (ResponseFeedback)
props.description: Offers an optional, dismissable "what was wrong" box after a Not helpful vote. Leave it out for no such step.

props.name: className (ResponseFeedback)
props.description: Goes on the group.

components.name: CodeBlock
components.summary: Code or a command in a panel, with a title bar that names the file or language and a button that copies the text. Long lines scroll sideways inside it, and code longer than one line gets line numbers.
components.useWhen: Showing code or a command someone will read or copy: an install step, a config file, an example.

props.name: code
props.description: The text shown and copied, exactly.

props.name: label
props.description: What the code is, in a few words ("the theme CSS"). Names the region and the copy button ("Copy the theme CSS").

props.name: title
props.description: Shown in the title bar: a file name ("index.css") or a language ("bash").

props.name: language
props.description: css colours comments, at-rules, selectors and property names; text is plain.

props.name: lineNumbers
props.description: Line numbers in a gutter. Unset, they show when the code has more than one line.

props.name: copyable
props.description: The copy button. Turn it off for code nobody should paste, such as a wrong example.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Wraps long lines instead of scrolling them sideways. For prose, such as a prompt; leave code unwrapped.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged onto the frame. Use it for width (max-w-3xl) and spacing.

props.name: ref
props.description: Passed through to the frame.

components.name: DatePicker
components.summary: One date, typed or picked. The field has a segment for the day, the month and the year, in the order your language writes them: type the digits and it moves on by itself, or use the arrow keys. The button inside it opens a calendar. The value is a plain 'YYYY-MM-DD' string with no time zone, so it means the same day for everyone. Calendar and DateField are exported too, for building your own.
components.useWhen: One date: a delivery day, a deadline, a birthday.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the field. Leave it out inside a FormField, which sets it from its own label. Outside one it is required, and `division-ds check` flags a missing one.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value (your page holds it).

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Starting value when the picker holds the value itself.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with a whole, real date, or '' when the field is emptied. A half-typed date does not fire.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest date, 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Earlier days are struck through; typing one marks the field invalid.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest date, 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

props.name: isDateDisabled
props.description: Days that cannot be picked, such as weekends or holidays.

props.name: locale
props.description: A language tag such as 'en-GB' or 'de'. Sets the segment order, the separator, the month and day names and the first day of the week. Defaults to the browser's.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: 0 Sunday to 6 Saturday. Defaults to the locale's.

props.name: showToday
props.description: Shows the Today button under the calendar when today can be picked.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field and the calendar button.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the 'YYYY-MM-DD' value with a form, through a hidden input.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the field invalid. FormField sets it when there is an error.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field required. FormField sets it.

props.name: id
props.description: The field's id, so a FormField's error text can point at it. FormField sets it.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: The ids of the help and error text. FormField sets it.

props.name: className
props.description: Combined with the field's classes.

props.name: ref
props.description: The field's group element.

props.name: trailing (DateField)
props.description: Something inside the field after the segments. DatePicker puts its calendar button here.

props.name: bare (DateField)
props.description: No border, fill or ring of its own, for two dates inside one border (DateRangePicker draws them).

props.name: onSelect (Calendar)
props.description: A day was picked with a click, Enter or Space.

props.name: value (Calendar)
props.description: The picked day. Ignored when dayState is given.

props.name: month (Calendar)
props.description: Any day in the first month shown. Controlled with onMonthChange.

props.name: defaultMonth (Calendar)
props.description: The first month shown when the calendar holds it itself. Defaults to the value's month, or today's.

props.name: onMonthChange (Calendar)
props.description: Fires with the new first month's 1st day.

props.name: dayState (Calendar)
props.description: Draws each day yourself, for a range or any other selection.

props.name: onDayEnter (Calendar)
props.description: The keyboard or the pointer moved onto a day. A range uses it to preview the band.

props.name: numberOfMonths (Calendar)
props.description: Months side by side, stacked on narrow screens.

props.name: autoFocus (Calendar)
props.description: Moves focus to the picked day, or today, when the calendar appears.

components.name: DatePresets
components.summary: Named periods such as Last 7 days, one click each. The defaults: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month, Last month, This year, or your own. An add-on: put it in a DateRangePicker's aside and it reads and sets the picker's range by itself, then closes it. On its own it is a list you give a value and an onSelect. Installs DateRangePicker and DatePicker with it.

props.name: presets
props.description: Each { label, range }. Make your own, or start from defaultPresets(today).

props.name: value
props.description: The current range. Inside a DateRangePicker it comes from the picker.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: A preset was chosen. Inside a DateRangePicker the picker also takes it and closes.

props.name: label
props.description: The list's accessible name.

props.name: ref
props.description: The list element.

components.name: DateRangePicker

Put DatePresets in `aside` for one-click periods like Last 7 days. Installs DatePicker with it.
components.useWhen: A booking, a report window, a leave request.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the field. Leave it out inside a FormField, which sets it from its own label. Outside one it is required, and `division-ds check` flags a missing one.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled range. Each end is 'YYYY-MM-DD' or ''.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Starting range when the picker holds it itself.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires when either end changes. Days picked in the calendar always arrive in order.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest date, 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest date, 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

props.name: isDateDisabled
props.description: Days that cannot be picked.

props.name: locale
props.description: Segment order, names and first day of the week. Defaults to the browser's.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: 0 Sunday to 6 Saturday. Defaults to the locale's.

props.name: aside
props.description: Beside the months, in the popover. DatePresets reads and sets the range by itself here.

props.name: partLabels
props.description: The names of the two dates.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables both dates and the button.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the field invalid. FormField sets it.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks both dates required. FormField sets it.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits name-start and name-end with a form.

props.name: id
props.description: The field's id. FormField sets it.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: The ids of the help and error text. FormField sets it.

props.name: className
props.description: Combined with the field's classes.

props.name: ref
props.description: The field's group element.

props.name: useDateRangePicker()
props.description: Inside the popover: the range, and a way to set it and close. For your own aside content.

components.name: DescriptionList
